questions.question: What happens when a muscle attached to a bone contracts?
options: It exerts a force on the bone, making the bone move.
It pushes the bone away from the joint.
It dissolves the bone tissue to release calcium.
It makes the bone temporarily flexible.

questions.question: Which scientific field is specifically defined as the study of how bones and muscles move?
options: Biochemistry
Biomechanics
Bioengineering
Biotechnology

questions.question: When a bone pivots at a joint, what is the turning effect of the force called?
options: A friction
A velocity
A moment
A tension

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the turning effect when a bone pivots at a joint?
options: The size of the moment cannot be measured or calculated.
The size of the moment can be calculated.
The moment is always constant regardless of the force applied.
The moment only depends on the weight of the bone itself.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about joints is true?
options: Bones are completely fused at all joints.
Joints are only found in the skull.
Joints prevent any movement in the body.
Bones meet at joints.

questions.question: What is the primary function of skeletal muscles in relation to bones?
options: They manufacture bone marrow.
They can move bones.
They act as a solid shield over the bones.
They absorb minerals from the bones.

questions.question: Why do skeletal muscles have to work in pairs to move a limb back and forth?
options: Muscles can only pull, by contracting, and cannot push.
Muscles can only push, by expanding, and cannot pull.
Muscles can only contract when they are compressed by another muscle.
One muscle is used for feeling pain and the other for movement.

questions.question: Muscles that work together in opposite directions to move bones at a joint are known as what?
options: Co-operative fibers
Symmetrical pairs
Antagonistic pairs
Auxiliary tissues

questions.question: Which statement is true about the muscular system in humans?
options: The human body contains muscles.
The human body is entirely made of bones with no muscles.
Muscles are only found in the limbs and not in the rest of the body.
Muscles are only present in adults and not in children.

questions.question: What type of biological structure is a muscle?
options: A single giant cell that stretches across the limb.
A type of tissue made up of specialised cells.
A non-cellular gel that hardens when stimulated.
An inorganic mineral structure.

questions.question: What are the two primary actions of muscle fibers?
options: Dissolve and rebuild
Freeze and melt
Calcify and soften
Contract and relax

questions.question: Which two substances must be supplied to muscles so that they can contract?
options: Carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Sugar and oxygen
Calcium and starch
Water and carbon dioxide

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists three different types of muscle found in human organ systems?
options: Rough muscle, smooth muscle and hard muscle
Brain muscle, lung muscle and bone muscle
Cardiac muscle, smooth muscle and skeletal muscle
Voluntary muscle, joint muscle and blood muscle

questions.question: What constitutes the human skeleton?
options: A framework made up of bones.
A network made up entirely of cartilage.
A system of fluid-filled tubes.
A series of hardened muscular bands.

questions.question: What is a joint in the human skeletal system?
options: The center of a long bone where blood is made.
The point where a muscle attaches to a tendon.
A place where two or more bones meet.
A protective layer of skin over a bone.

questions.question: Which of these is a key function of the human skeleton?
options: It produces digestive enzymes to break down food.
It pumps oxygenated blood directly to the brain.
It stores carbon dioxide waste from respiration.
It supports the body and provides protection for organs and tissues.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the structure of human bones?
options: Bones are made of living tissue made up of cells.
Bones are dead, dry structures containing no cells.
Bones are solid blocks of pure calcium with no living parts.
Bones are made of cartilage that never contains cells.

questions.question: Where in the human body are red and white blood cells produced?
options: In the liver tissue
In the bone marrow
In the heart chambers
In the skeletal muscles
